#


Infura vs Alchemy vs Quicknode: 2026 Deep-Dive Comparison


Infura vs Alchemy vs Quicknode compared for 2026: chain support, pricing, real-world cost scenarios, features, performance, and compliance. See which RPC provider fits your workload.


[Quicknode](https://www.quicknode.com/blog/author/quicknode)


July 7, 2026 — 5 min read


Infura, Alchemy, and[Quicknode](https://www.quicknode.com/?utm_source=blog&utm_campaign=comparison&utm_medium=blog&utm_content=infura-alchemy-quicknode) are three of the most widely used blockchain infrastructure providers. This guide compares chain support, cost at real traffic, performance, and what you get beyond a raw RPC endpoint, with numbers verified in August 2026.


**Short version:** Infura is the Ethereum-native option with MetaMask ties and daily-quota billing. Alchemy has the most generous ongoing free tier and the strongest built-in developer APIs. Quicknode covers the most production ground: 80+ chains, archive on every plan, trace on paid plans, real-time[Streams](https://www.quicknode.com/streams) , the lowest latency in its own public QuickLee benchmarks, and the only full SOC 1, SOC 2, and ISO 27001 stack of the three.


## Infura vs Alchemy vs Quicknode at a glance


-


Free tier: Quicknode 1-month trial, 10M API credits; Alchemy 30M CU/mo ongoing; Infura 3M credits/day ongoing


-


Entry paid: Quicknode Build $49/mo; Alchemy Pay As You Go; Infura Developer $50/mo


-


Chains: Quicknode 80+ / 135+ networks; Alchemy 79 chains; Infura ~24 chains, 40+ networks


-


Trace/debug: Quicknode paid plans at 2x credits; Alchemy Pay As You Go+; Infura Developer+


-


Real-time: Quicknode Streams, Webhooks, gRPC; Alchemy Webhooks and Smart WebSockets; Infura WebSocket RPC


-


Compliance: Quicknode SOC 1, SOC 2, ISO 27001; Alchemy SOC 2 Type II; Infura not published


## How each provider bills


**One request is not one request.** Quicknode bills API credits (eth_call is 20 on most EVM chains). Alchemy bills compute units (eth_call is 26 CUs). Infura bills credits against a daily quota that resets at 00:00 UTC. A spike can halt Infura until the next reset.


True cost per call = (method weight x price per million units) / 1,000,000. Two providers can advertise the same price per million and still differ 4x on your bill.


## Chain support


Alchemy’s RPC directory lists 79 chains, in line with Quicknode’s 80+. Alchemy’s “100+ networks” headline counts testnets. Infura covers ~24 chains and 40+ networks, including Monad and HyperEVM; Solana is limited-access. Quicknode’s edge is Bitcoin, TRON, TON, and Hyperliquid HyperCore/gRPC under one account, plus archive and Streams. See the[Quicknode chain list](https://www.quicknode.com/chains) .


## Pricing compared (2026)


**Quicknode:** 1-month trial at $0 (10M credits, 15 rps), then Build $49 / 80M / 50 rps, Accelerate $249 / 450M / 125, Scale $499 / 950M / 250, Business $999 / 2B / 500 rps. Overage $0.62/1M credits on Build to $0.50 on Business. Archive on every plan including trial; trace/debug on paid plans at 2x.[Flat Rate RPS](https://www.quicknode.com/docs/platform/billing/flat-rate-rps) starts at $799/mo for 75 RPS on ETH/Base/OP/Arb/BSC/Polygon (Solana $1,199). Over cap returns HTTP 429.


**Alchemy:** ongoing Free 30M CU/mo at 25 rps, then Pay As You Go at $0.45/1M CU to 300M, then $0.40. Debug/trace not on Free. eth_getLogs is 60 CUs (~$27/1M); debug_traceTransaction is 40 CUs (~$18/1M), cheaper than Quicknode’s 2x paid trace rate (~$24.80/1M on Build overage).


**Infura:** Core $0 at 3M credits/day; Developer $50 at 15M/day; Team $225 at 75M/day. eth_call is 80 credits, eth_getLogs 255, debug_traceTransaction 1,000 (15,000 traces/day on Developer). Extra credits $200 for 55M.


## Real-world monthly cost (read-heavy eth_call)


-


500K: Quicknode $0 during 1-month trial, then $49 Build; Alchemy $0; Infura $0


-


5M: Quicknode ~$61; Alchemy ~$59; Infura $50


-


25M: Quicknode ~$277; Alchemy ~$275; Infura $225


-


100M: Quicknode $999 Business; Alchemy ~$1,055; Infura Enterprise


-


500M: Quicknode Enterprise / Flat Rate RPS; Alchemy ~$5,200; Infura Enterprise


Log-heavy apps pay more on Alchemy. Trace-heavy apps often pay less on Alchemy than Quicknode. Infura traces still exhaust a Developer day fast. Streams destinations are webhook, S3, PostgreSQL, Azure Blob, and Kafka.


## Beyond raw RPC


-


**Alchemy** has the broadest first-party APIs (Token, NFT, Transfers, Portfolio, Prices, Wallet, Paymaster, Bundler) plus webhooks. Subgraphs sunset December 8, 2025.


-


**Infura** wins on MetaMask proximity, a Gas API, and DIN failover. No Streams equivalent. IPFS is restricted to pre-qualified customers.


-


**Quicknode** bundles Streams, Webhooks, SQL Explorer, Marketplace add-ons, Yellowstone gRPC, Hyperliquid gRPC, IPFS, and x402/MPP.


## Performance


In Quicknode’s public[QuickLee](https://www.quicknode.com/blog/quicklee-v2) dashboards (eth_getBalance every 10 seconds, five regions), Quicknode has published ~29ms average and ~45ms p95 with zero failed calls across ~148K requests. Treat QuickLee as a live dataset, not a universal ranking.


## Which provider should you choose?


-


**DeFi and trading bots:** Quicknode, plus[Flat Rate RPS](https://www.quicknode.com/docs/platform/billing/flat-rate-rps) to remove overage on continuous polling.


-


**Enterprise and regulated apps:** Quicknode. Full SOC 1, SOC 2, and ISO 27001 plus 99.99% uptime. Alchemy publishes SOC 2 Type II; Infura does not publish SOC or ISO.


-


**Ethereum-only / MetaMask:** Infura. Early-stage teams also fit Alchemy’s ongoing 30M free CUs or the[Quicknode Startup Program](https://www.quicknode.com/startup) .


-


**API-heavy prototyping:** Alchemy. Ongoing free tier, 79 chains, and first-party Token/NFT/Transfers APIs.


-


**Multi-chain and AI agents:** Quicknode. 80+ chains, plus x402/MPP and an MCP server.


## Frequently asked questions


### Does Quicknode have a free plan?


Quicknode offers a 1-month free trial with 10M API credits and 15 rps. It is not an ongoing free tier. Alchemy’s 30M CU/mo and Infura’s 3M credits/day remain available month after month. After the trial, paid plans start at $49/mo on Build.


### How many chains does each provider support?


As of August 2026, Quicknode supports 80+ chains across 135+ networks. Alchemy lists 79 chains on alchemy.com/rpc; the “100+ networks” headline counts testnets. Infura covers roughly 24 chains and 40+ networks.


### Which providers are SOC 2 certified?


Quicknode (SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001) and Alchemy (SOC 2 Type II) publish certifications. Infura does not. Quicknode is the only provider here with all three.
